title: Microscopic Insights into the Quarkyonic Hadron--Quark Crossover: Lessons from Ultracold Fermi Gases
abstract: In neutron-star and dense quantum chromodynamics (QCD) physics, it is important to understand how baryonic matter evolves into quark matter at high density. A continuous hadron--quark crossover is one of the most attractive candidates because it can reconcile the comparatively soft equation of state around nuclear density with the rapid stiffening required to support massive neutron stars. Recent neutron-star observations motivate equations of state that stiffen rapidly across the intermediate-density regime, while quarkyonic-matter descriptions feature a shell-like baryon momentum distribution there. In this paper, we review our recent work on the microscopic description and interpretation of these phenomena by drawing an analogy with the Bose--Einstein condensate (BEC) to Bardeen--Cooper--Schrieffer (BCS) crossover in ultracold Fermi gases and two-color QCD. As pairing fluctuations play a crucial role in the BEC--BCS crossover, we discuss the role of its three-body counterpart, that is, tripling fluctuations associated with baryon formation in the hadron--quark crossover. In terms of a phase-shift representation of tripling fluctuations, the interplay between a three-body bound-state pole and the scattering continuum suppresses low-momentum baryonic occupation, generates a baryonic momentum shell, and reduces the density susceptibility, thereby producing a peak in the speed of sound. We review the demonstration of this mechanism in a one-dimensional three-component Fermi gas, its relativistic extension, and its connection to phenomenological quarkyonic equations of state.
summary: This paper develops a theoretical framework by mapping the hadron-quark crossover onto the physics of three-body crossovers seen in ultracold Fermi gases. It demonstrates that the mechanism causing a momentum shell formation—the interplay between bound states and the continuum—is responsible for predicting a characteristic peak in the speed of sound in dense QCD matter. This provides a concrete, calculable link between cold atom physics and astrophysics.
main_problem: The paper addresses the challenge of understanding the continuous crossover from hadronic matter to quark matter at high baryon density.
main_result: The authors show that the interplay between a three-body bound-state pole and the scattering continuum generates a baryonic momentum shell, which in turn causes a peak in the speed of sound in the crossover region.
method: The analysis employs fluctuation theory, drawing an analogy between the BEC-BCS crossover in ultracold Fermi gases and the three-body crossover in dense QCD matter.
model_or_system: The model uses a three-component Fermi gas with an attractive three-body contact interaction to simulate the baryon formation process, connecting it to quarkyonic matter.
key_observables: Speed of sound ($c_s^2$), baryonic momentum distribution ($f_B(K)$), and the in-medium three-body binding energy ($B_M$).
important_parameters: High baryon density, low temperatures, and the three-body coupling strength ($V_3$).
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on the pole-continuum cancellation mechanism and approximations regarding the occupied continuum weight.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the momentum distributions of quark and baryon constituents, and plot the squared isothermal speed of sound, showing a pronounced maximum in the crossover region.
paper_structure: The paper reviews the theoretical framework by first establishing the BEC-BCS analogy, then developing the three-body fluctuation theory using T-matrix calculations, and finally applying this mechanism to predict observable features like the momentum shell and speed of sound peak in the context of QCD.
why_interesting: The direct analogy drawn between the well-understood BEC-BCS crossover in ultracold atoms and the exotic physics of the hadron-quark crossover provides a powerful, calculable theoretical tool for condensed matter/AMO theorists.
